prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: 리비아 country-learning postcard for a children's world atlas.
Primary request / scene: Leptis Magna on Libya's Mediterranean coast. A believable ancient Roman archaeological landscape of pale honey limestone: a broad paved avenue flanked by surviving weathered columns and low ruined walls, a substantial preserved four-sided Roman triumphal arch farther along the avenue, archaeological stone fragments at the sides. A narrow distant Mediterranean blue horizon and flat dry coastal terrain. No single intact fantasy palace, no Egyptian pyramids, no mountain range, no modern skyscrapers or reconstruction of every ruin as new. Spacious three-quarter view with real ruin character, worn stone, broken columns and clear depth.
Style/medium: Warm bright detailed children's travel-book illustration matching the atlas's Korean hanok and Great Wall paintings: soft watercolour washes, opaque gouache brushwork, fine coloured-pencil detail, tactile painted paper, luminous cream clouds and blue sky, gently saturated greens and teal, warm ochre and terracotta. Believable landscape/landmark geometry, simplified just enough for young children. Not photographic, not flat vector or sticker art.
Composition/framing: One independent full-bleed landscape image, exact 3:2 aspect ratio, intended 1536x1024. A clear layered foreground, midground and background; the key scene remains readable on a small card, inside the frame with breathing room. No collage.
Lighting/mood: Welcoming warm natural daylight, cheerful and calm.
Constraints: No text, letters, writing, signs, flags, coats of arms, maps, logos, watermark, borders, stamps or UI. No invented landmarks or unrelated scenery.
inspection: Weathered Roman columns, paved avenue, preserved arch and surrounding ruins with dry coastal terrain; no pyramids or complete fantasy palace. Monument details are illustrative rather than measured.
